narrative.old: `models all` catalog and `candy-code login [provider]` (Codex PKCE) have shipped (a Claude subscription can ride the CLI's own login via the `bare: false` provider option)
narrative.new: No native subscription OAuth (`candy-code login` hands off to `claude auth login` / `codex login` or stores an API key); no Azure or OpenRouter type, no OpenAI Responses API, no OS keychain

narrative.old: First prompt build of a session, memoised; re-read only on `/clear`, compaction, rewind or a session switch
narrative.new: First prompt build of a session, memoised; re-spliced only on `/clear`, compaction, rewind or a session switch. Mid-session edits reach the model next turn as a bounded diff in the `<turn-context>` tail

narrative.old: `/context` text only
narrative.new: Context panel: instruction files with path, size and tier, refused files under "Not read", memory, skills, MCP; `/context` text too

narrative.old: `/init` (TUI only) | ❌ refused (`ui_only`)
narrative.new: `/init` (TUI and served) | ✅ typed `/init` runs on the host

narrative.old: Its nested path is now fenced and fork-safe. What remains is *visibility*: no tool lists the loaded files at startup (Claude Code only notes AGENTS.md and size warnings), and candy-code doesn't even name them in `/context`.
narrative.new: Its nested path is fenced and fork-safe, and it is also the most *visible*: the startup summary and `/context` name the loaded files, the web Context panel lists them, and `instructionsExclude` silences a file with a recorded refusal. What it lacks is an in-app editor for instruction files and a trust gate.

narrative.old: Claude Code and OpenClaw at least name the files on demand (`/memory`, `/context list`).
narrative.new: Claude Code and OpenClaw also name the files on demand (`/memory`, `/context list`), and both can open them for editing, which candy-code cannot.

narrative.old: 🟡 Notices for auto/dream writes and for the flush (names its saved rows); recall stays unannounced
narrative.new: ✅ Notices for auto/dream writes and the flush (names its saved rows) plus a per-turn "Recalled N notes" row (count only; TUI only, since serve never drains the notice sink)

narrative.old: `/memory list/add/search/edit/delete/log/restore` (text)
narrative.new: `/memory list/add/search/edit/delete/clear/import/log/restore` (text) + `/memory open <id>` in `$EDITOR`

narrative.old: Claude Code's memory is simpler but the most *transparent*: it says when it saved or recalled something.
narrative.new: Claude Code's memory is simpler but the most *transparent*: its saved/recalled rows link the files. candy-code's TUI also reports saves and a recall count, but the web shows neither.

narrative.old: Provenance labels were fixed (user and model notes in the repo store carry the right author, and the memory slot refreshes after `/memory add`).
narrative.new: User and model notes in the repo store carry their own author labels, and the memory slot refreshes after `/memory add`.

narrative.old: coder, reviewer, debugger, architect, tester, devops (⚠ coder lacks Write; tester lacks Write+Edit) | runs only
narrative.new: coder, reviewer, debugger, architect, tester, devops (coder and tester carry Write/Edit/Grep/Glob) | runs + Agent catalog panel

narrative.old: ⚠ Names only ("Current agent roster: architect, coder, …")
narrative.new: ✅ Fenced `<available-agents>` roster in the Task guidance: name, description, tools summary, source badge

narrative.old: Agents panel = this session's runs; catalog unused
narrative.new: Agents panel = this session's runs; Agent catalog panel (`agents.list`) lists every preset with model and mode

narrative.old: For *finding* them the model still sees names only, though the user-facing gap closed on 2026-10-18: `/agents` now lists the full roster with descriptions.
narrative.new: For *finding* them it is at parity: the model gets a fenced roster with descriptions and tools, `/agents` lists the full roster, and the web has a catalog panel; only `@agent` mentions and an agent wizard are missing.

narrative.old: Each step also gets a user-role `<turn-context>` tail: git status/diff after writes, changed-since-read files, memory recall, context % past 60 %, post-compaction re-injection.
narrative.new: Each step also gets a user-role `<turn-context>` tail: git status/diff after writes, changed-since-read files, instruction-file diffs, memory recall, context % past 60 %, post-compaction re-injection.

narrative.old: Explicit cache breakpoints exist only for Claude-on-Vertex and Bedrock. ⚠ The `anthropic` provider uses Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which **does not cache**.
narrative.new: Explicit cache breakpoints on the native `anthropic` arm and Claude-on-Vertex (`CacheBreakpoints`, ≤4 marks) and Bedrock (`cachePoint`); OpenAI and SGLang cache prefixes server-side; `CacheHealthWatch` warns on repeated zero-cache replies.

narrative.old: Three figures: calibrated status-bar estimate, provider-anchored in-turn budget, and ⚠ history-only text estimate for the 70/85/95 % tiers (misses system prompt + tool schemas, so tiers fire late)
narrative.new: Script-weighted estimate calibrated against provider-reported usage; the 70/85/95 % tiers and the status bar read the same calibrated figure (system prompt, tool schemas and tool arguments included); the in-turn step budget is provider-anchored

narrative.old: Tiers 70/85/95 %, absolute caps 100k/150k, in-turn step budget, overflow retry
narrative.new: Tiers 70/85/95 %, absolute caps 100k/150k, in-turn step budget, overflow retry; opt-in idle fold (`compaction.idleAuto`) after an hour idle

narrative.old: Model summary with six facets + merged `<session-state>`; summaries **pre-fetched ahead of need** using the cached prefix; re-inject files, plan, skills, git, todos
narrative.new: Model summary with six facets + merged `<session-state>`; summaries **pre-fetched ahead of need** using the cached prefix; `SummarySafeguard` audits headings, asks and identifiers (HOLD → heuristic fold); re-inject files, plan, skills, git, todos

narrative.old: 6. **One-per-turn "Recalled N notes" row** — count-only, uiOnly, riding the `RuntimeNoticeSink` pipeline with zero renderer work.
narrative.new: 6. **One-per-turn "Recalled N notes" row** — count-only, uiOnly, riding the `RuntimeNoticeSink` pipeline with zero renderer work (TUI only: `serve` arms the sink but nothing drains it).
